Test never checks reconstructed DER is original signature or verifies with keyPair.getPublic(). Verify asn1Des with public key so test detects conversions consumers cannot validate.

integerToBytes silently truncates oversized r/s values. When DER signature carries r or s integer longer than signLength/2 bytes and extra leading bytes are not just sign-byte zero, integerToBytes drops high-order bytes. asn1derToConcatenatedRS returns different well-formed r/s pair instead of rejecting malformed signature.

Malformed DER throws unchecked exceptions instead of IOException. Zero-length INTEGER causes readInteger to call new BigInteger(new byte[0]) throwing NumberFormatException. Indefinite length (0x80) causes readLength to return -1 and readNext can produce negative array size.

Equal-order providers are now picked silently. detectProvider used to fail fast when several CryptoProviders were on classpath, now sorts by order() and takes first one. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. If two present, choice depends on ServiceLoader discovery order, so non-FIPS provider may be selected unexpectedly.

The all-clients resource is considered only when the client-specific resource is absent. Once any per-client resource exists (for example, because a different scope was granted to this client), a grant on the Clients resource is never evaluated, so an all-clients manage/view/other scope does not apply to that client. Evaluate both applicable resources (or fall back to the all-clients resource when the specific evaluation does not grant the requested scope).

This returns the schema resource name (Clients) as though it were a client ID whenever a permission is granted on the all-clients resource. AvailableRoleMappingResource then calls realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream() for every returned value, so an all-clients grant causes a null dereference (and the grant cannot correctly identify the affected clients). The all-clients resource should be handled separately by expanding to the realm's clients, while only per-client resources should contribute their client IDs.

Removal listener is gated on the V1 feature flag, which breaks V2 cleanup and V1+V2 client deletion. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, the new Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard skips all role, client and group cleanup, so per-client permission resources stay behind after a client is deleted.

The all-clients grant is considered only when the client-specific resource is absent. Once a client resource exists (for example after a client-specific authorization lookup/creation), a grant attached to the Clients resource is never evaluated, so users authorized for all clients are denied for that client. Evaluate the all-clients resource as an additional fallback/alternative rather than making it mutually exclusive with the per-client resource.

getResourceTypeResource explicitly returns null when the authorization schema/resource is not provisioned, but the result is passed directly to findByResource. In that state this permission check throws instead of denying access. Check resource == null before querying the policy store (and before constructing the ResourcePermission).

This evaluator is now returned by MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(), but the existing client-management endpoint still calls these methods at ClientResource's GET/PUT management/permissions paths. With V2 enabled, those requests now throw UnsupportedOperationException and return a server error instead of a response. Either implement the endpoint's contract for V2 or prevent these paths from selecting this evaluator.

This mutates the class-scoped myclient fixture, but onAfter() only removes authorization permissions and does not restore client state. Since @InjectRealm defaults to LifeCycle.CLASS, a later test that looks up findByClientId("myclient") can get an empty result (or the evaluator can resolve a different resource), making the suite order-dependent; the default-scope removal/addition in this same test also changes the shared client. Register a cleanup that restores the original client representation and scope assignments, or isolate/reset the realm per test.

The test deletes the client it creates, but it does not clean up the two client roles created in testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, nor restore the default/optional scope assignments changed in testManageOnlyOneClient. These objects belong to the class-scoped managed realm and onAfter() removes only permissions, so later methods run against accumulated realm state rather than the fixture described by their assertions.

getClientsWithPermission uses findByType, which does not match per-client resources. resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) only returns resources whose type is "Clients". AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources without setType, so only the all-clients type resource (named "Clients") has that type.

canView() ignores MANAGE or CONFIGURE on all clients. When an admin holds only an all-clients MANAGE permission, canView() returns false because it checks only canViewClientDefault() or hasPermission(VIEW). canView(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientModel) do accept MANAGE, so the three are inconsistent.

A per-client resource hides the all-clients permission. When a client already has its own resource, for example from a CONFIGURE permission on it, hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) evaluates only that resource. An all-clients MANAGE, VIEW or MAP_ROLES permission is not consulted, so canManage(client) returns false for an admin who holds MANAGE on all clients.

The user search filter expects actual GroupModel IDs, but the code adds the authorization resource's internal ID instead. getOrCreateResource creates resources whose name is the group ID, while the resource ID is a separate authorization-store identifier, causing users in permitted groups to be omitted from searches

With the new V2 group evaluator, the set contains authorization resource IDs instead of GroupModel IDs. GroupPermissionsV2 adds groupResource.getId(), while the user provider compares UserModel.GROUPS directly with UserGroupMembershipEntity.groupId, filtering out users who have group-scoped view-members permission

The parameterless canManage() method treats the VIEW scope as sufficient for management. GroupsResource uses this method in requireManage() for mutating group operations, allowing administrators with only global view permission to perform writes

canManage() treats the view scope as sufficient for managing groups, allowing administrators granted only the Groups view policy to pass the collection-level manage check and reach mutation endpoints. Should restrict to AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE only

This V2 evaluator is selected by MgmtPermissionsV2.groups(), but the existing group management-permissions endpoint still calls isPermissionsEnabled(group). With V2 enabled, GET /groups/{id}/management/permissions throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a response. The inherited resource() and getPermissions() methods also throw and need V2-safe implementations

Message resource uses Java MessageFormat placeholders ({0}, {1}, {2,choice,...}) but is consumed by i18next backend which expects {{name}} interpolation syntax, causing literal placeholder text to render instead of actual values
Anchor removal logic bypasses POLICY_SOME_HTML sanitization for English source messages, allowing unsafe anchors like <a href="javascript:..."> to pass validation unchecked
Lithuanian totpStep1 resource contains Italian text instead of Lithuanian translation, showing wrong language to Lithuanian users
Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 resource contains Italian text instead of Lithuanian translation
Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 contains Traditional Chinese characters, mixing scripts inconsistently with other Simplified Chinese messages
Diff-position computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBounds when sanitized differs from value by removing characters that equal their neighbours, causing start and end indices to overlap

Access-token creation fails for internal callers that do not set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the client-session context - PolicyEvaluationService and KeycloakIdentity call createClientAccessToken directly without the grant attribute being populated, causing encodeTokenId to throw IllegalStateException

grantType is cached only in the constructor but setFormParams(...) allows callers to replace request parameters without updating this field, causing incorrect access-token context when grant implementations change form parameters before token creation
The second null check validates grantType again instead of rawTokenId, allowing null raw ID to be accepted and encodeTokenId to concatenate it as literal 'null', causing ID collisions

Registry accepts provider shortcuts without enforcing the two-character format assumed by encoder/decoder - custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning null or non-two-character shortcuts produces IDs that cannot be decoded, and duplicate shortcuts silently overwrite the forward map

Lazy registration path bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation performed in postInit, allowing shortcuts to overwrite existing grantsByShortcuts entries and causing previously issued IDs to be reinterpreted incorrectly

Client-credentials flow never stores its grant type on ClientSessionContext - ClientCredentialsGrantType.process() builds access token directly without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE, so the 'cc' shortcut is never used
Test catches every RuntimeException instead of the expected IllegalArgumentException, allowing unrelated failures to pass the test without specifically verifying rejection of unknown grant shortcut
rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead - Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') repeats the grantType check and never checks rawTokenId
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong offsets - substring(3, 5) returns false on match and uses wrong slice positions; grant shortcut should be at substring(4, 6)

A successful federated recovery-code validation only checks membership and leaves the matched value in myUser.recoveryCodes - the same code can be submitted repeatedly and remains valid indefinitely. Remove the matched code and persist the updated serialized list as part of successful validation.

When the matching credential comes from user storage, the helper returns its federated model, but removeStoredCredentialById only removes from the local credential store. After the last recovery code is consumed, the exhausted federated credential is left in user storage and is not removed as expected.

A malformed federated recovery credential is silently removed from the returned stream after only a generic log message. A deserialization failure is indistinguishable from 'no federated credential' and can cause an unrelated local credential to be selected. Preserve the failure/credential state or prevent fallback when the provider has a malformed recovery credential, and include exception context in the diagnostic.

Recovery credentials are reported as configured, but disableCredentialType still only clears OTP and logs recovery codes as unsupported. Deleting/disabling this federated credential through the credential manager/admin path leaves myUser.recoveryCodes intact and the credential remains usable.

Raw recovery codes sent to user storage in a format the consumers can't read - createRecoveryCodesCredential passes the plaintext generatedCodes JSON as the UserCredentialModel challengeResponse while the hashed credentialModel (credentialData and secretData) is discarded.

Federated credential passed to local-store removal when all codes are used - RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential prefers the federated credential, but when it reports allCodesUsed(), removeStoredCredentialById is called which only operates on the local credential store. A federated model's id is either storage-specific or null.

The test never waits for the reader thread to finish before checking caughtExceptions. The main thread can delete the groups, set the flag, and assert while the reader has not yet executed (or has not yet recorded) an exception, so a regression that throws during groups(...) can pass; the thread may also record an exception after the assertion.
